Use `snl batch check` to preflight a dependent multi-entity change set without writing.

### Command path
`batch/check` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The shell adapter is `snl batch check`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"batch/check","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{"input":"<file|->"}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. Schema, syntax/semantic, and workspace-reference diagnostics remain distinguishable.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"batch/check","data":...,"diagnostics":[]}`. `data` contains normalized identity when available and stable-code diagnostics; `ok:true` means no error-severity diagnostic.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"batch/check","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":...,"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Read-only. It must not create temp files inside `.SNL_Doc`, acquire a writer lock, or repair the draft. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. Repeated calls against unchanged bytes return equivalent semantic results.
